# ARC Stream Puzzle Solving

Use this workflow for ARC-style tasks where each instance presents an input grid and may allow additional demonstration pairs.

## Workflow

1. **Parse the grid exactly.** Record dimensions, colors, object boundaries, symmetries, and connected components. Keep the input available as a literal matrix; output grids often preserve most cells unchanged.
2. **Inspect each demonstration as a before/after diff.** List every changed coordinate and its old/new value. Compare changed regions with unchanged structures to identify a conditional transformation, rather than guessing from appearance.
3. **Generate competing rule hypotheses.** Check whether changes depend on shape, adjacency, alignment, component size, position, or a special marker/color. Verify each hypothesis against changed and unchanged parts of all available demos.
4. **Request another demo when it will resolve a real ambiguity.** Identify candidate rules that predict different outcomes, then seek evidence that discriminates between them. Each request costs a point; do not use requests just to defer deciding. If still underdetermined, a targeted new example is preferable to an unsupported submission.
5. **Apply the inferred rule mechanically to the test grid.** Preserve unaffected cells and dimensions. Change only cells compelled by the rule. Validate row lengths and allowed values before submitting.
6. **After incorrect feedback, revise the hypothesis.** Do not repeat the same transformation. Use remaining demos to distinguish alternatives and carefully re-check the application.

## Pitfalls

Use this workflow for ARC-style tasks where each instance presents an input grid and may allow additional demonstration pairs.
